evals.prompt: I'm building a Flutter app and need a solid auth flow. Users sign in with email/password via Supabase. I need to handle token refresh, persist the session securely, and make sure the auth state drives the router (so unauthenticated users can't access protected screens). What's the right architecture and show me the core code?
evals.expected_output: Architectural blueprint explaining data flow, then complete BLoC/Cubit + Repository code with secure token storage (flutter_secure_storage), token refresh logic, and router guard driven by auth stream. Ends with Architectural Verification bullets covering security, state safety, and edge cases (token expiry, process death, concurrent refresh).

assertions.name: includes-architectural-blueprint
assertions.description: Response contains an 'Architectural Blueprint' section with prose explanation before any code

assertions.name: uses-secure-storage
assertions.description: Code uses flutter_secure_storage or platform Keychain/Keystore — never SharedPreferences for tokens

assertions.name: no-todo-placeholders
assertions.description: No // TODO or // implement later comments in the code

assertions.name: includes-architectural-verification
assertions.description: Response ends with an 'Architectural Verification' bullet list

assertions.name: handles-token-refresh
assertions.description: Token refresh / expiry edge case is addressed in code or verification

evals.prompt: We're building a React Native field-service app. Technicians use it in tunnels and basements with zero connectivity. All job data must be readable and writable offline, then synced to the backend (a REST API) when connectivity resumes. Conflicts should be handled. Walk me through the architecture and give me the core sync engine code.
evals.expected_output: Blueprint covering offline-first strategy (local DB as source of truth, sync queue, conflict resolution approach). Core code for the sync engine with exponential backoff, operation queuing, and conflict handling. Verification bullets covering network failure, concurrent writes, process death mid-sync.

assertions.name: includes-architectural-blueprint
assertions.description: Response has a prose Architectural Blueprint section

assertions.name: addresses-conflict-resolution
assertions.description: Conflict resolution strategy is described and/or implemented

assertions.name: uses-retry-backoff
assertions.description: Exponential backoff or retry logic is present in the sync engine

assertions.name: no-todo-placeholders
assertions.description: No // TODO or placeholder comments

assertions.name: includes-architectural-verification
assertions.description: Architectural Verification bullets are present at the end

evals.prompt: I'm using Flutter with Isar as the local database. I need to store user profile data and sensitive financial records. What's the right way to encrypt the sensitive fields, set up the Isar schema, and make sure the data layer is cleanly separated from my UI? Show me the full pattern.
evals.expected_output: Blueprint covering encryption approach (field-level vs full-DB, key management via Keychain/Keystore), Isar schema code with proper typing, repository pattern implementation. Verification bullets covering key storage, migration, and null safety.

assertions.name: uses-secure-key-storage

assertions.name: repository-pattern-present
assertions.description: A repository class or interface is shown that abstracts the Isar data source from the domain

assertions.name: no-dynamic-types

evals.prompt: I'm building a SwiftUI iOS app (iOS 16+) with The Composable Architecture (TCA). I need a feature that shows a paginated list of products fetched from a REST API, supports pull-to-refresh, handles errors gracefully with a retry button, and stores the last successful response in CoreData so the list is available offline. Show me the TCA feature structure and the full implementation.
evals.expected_output: Blueprint explaining TCA unidirectional flow (Action -> Reducer -> Effect -> State), CoreData stack setup, pagination logic. Complete Swift code: State/Action/Reducer/Effect for the feature, CoreData entity, repository protocol and implementation. Verification bullets covering offline availability, pagination edge cases, error recovery, and memory safety.

assertions.name: includes-architectural-blueprint

assertions.name: uses-tca-pattern
assertions.description: Code uses TCA State/Action/Reducer structure (or equivalent composable architecture pattern)

assertions.name: handles-offline-with-coredata
assertions.description: CoreData (or SwiftData) is used for offline persistence and referenced in code or verification

assertions.name: no-todo-placeholders
assertions.description: No // TODO or placeholder comments in Swift code

assertions.name: includes-architectural-verification
assertions.description: Architectural Verification bullets at the end covering edge cases

evals.prompt: We have a Flutter app (iOS + Android) and a React Native app (iOS + Android) — four targets total. We need a CI/CD pipeline that: runs unit and widget/component tests on every PR, builds signed release artifacts (IPA and AAB) on merge to main, deploys to TestFlight and Google Play internal track automatically, and sends a Slack notification on success or failure. We use GitHub Actions. Design the full pipeline architecture and give me the key workflow YAML.
evals.expected_output: Blueprint explaining the pipeline stages and secret management strategy. GitHub Actions YAML for both Flutter and RN covering: test job, build job (with signing), deploy job (TestFlight via fastlane/xcrun, Play via fastlane supply or google-github-actions), Slack notification step. Verification bullets covering secret isolation, signing key security, and failure handling.

assertions.name: includes-architectural-blueprint
assertions.description: Prose blueprint explaining pipeline stages and secret strategy present

assertions.name: covers-signing-secrets
assertions.description: Signing certificates/keys are handled via GitHub Secrets or a secrets manager — not hardcoded

assertions.name: includes-testflight-and-play-deploy
assertions.description: Both TestFlight (iOS) and Google Play (Android) deployment steps are present

assertions.name: includes-slack-notification
assertions.description: Slack notification step on success and/or failure is included

assertions.name: includes-architectural-verification
assertions.description: Architectural Verification bullets present at the end
